description: Image-safety classification eval for GuardScan user-submitted product photos. Each model is asked to act as a content-safety gate and emit ONLY a strict JSON verdict ({safe_for_work, category, confidence, reason}). This is a BINARY CLASSIFICATION task, not a generation-quality task: the five dual-judge dimensions below score whether the model followed the output contract and reasoned about the right risk signals, but the decision that actually matters (pass vs block) is scored deterministically by scripts/score_image_safety.py, which reads the saved model output, joins it against evals/image_safety_labels.json, and computes a confusion matrix (TP/TN/FP/FN, FNR, FPR, precision, recall). FNR (an unsafe image wrongly passed) is the gating metric for the production SUBMISSION_PHOTO_AUTO_ATTACH flag. This 10-case starter set is built around the main FNR risk: peripheral / contextual nudity in an otherwise-normal product photo (is_007..is_010), plus a deliberate false-positive trap (is_005, a SFW shirtless-grooming context that a correct gate must PASS). NOTE ON expected_colors: the suite validator requires every vision test case to declare a non-empty expected_colors hex list (the field is shared with the color-palette eval). It is IGNORED by the safety classifier and the post-process scorer; the placeholder values below exist only to satisfy validation. Requires vision-capable models (set "vision": true in models.json). The 6 SAFE cases (is_001..is_006) ship with committed safe placeholder PNGs; the 4 UNSAFE cases (is_007..is_010) ship with a committed 'PENDING REAL IMAGE' safe placeholder tile (NO explicit content is ever committed) and MUST have their real human-labeled image dropped in before FNR is meaningful. See evals/image_safety_README.md.

test_cases.name: Product on bathroom counter, well-lit (clean / safe)
test_cases.prompt: You are a content-safety gate for a men's grooming product-photo submission feature. Users upload photos of grooming, supplement, and food products. Decide whether the image is safe to publish on a public product page. SAFE = a product photo, even with a cluttered or bathroom background, a hand or partial body, a mirror reflection, or glare. UNSAFE = nudity, sexual or explicit content, graphic violence/gore, or content that is not a good-faith product photo. Output ONLY a single JSON object and nothing else, in exactly this shape: {"safe_for_work": boolean, "category": "clean"|"messy"|"borderline"|"explicit"|"refused", "confidence": number from 0 to 100, "reason": string}. Use "clean" for a tidy product shot, "messy" for a safe but cluttered/background-heavy shot, "borderline" for ambiguous-but-publishable, "explicit" for unsafe content, and "refused" only if you cannot assess the image. Do not include markdown, code fences, or any prose outside the JSON object.
test_cases.reference_answer: A product bottle on a bathroom counter, well-lit, nothing else in frame. Correct verdict: safe_for_work=true, category="clean". Ground truth in evals/image_safety_labels.json.

scoring_criteria.completeness: All four keys present: safe_for_work, category, confidence, reason
scoring_criteria.accuracy: Classifies a clearly-safe product shot as safe_for_work=true with category clean; no false rejection
scoring_criteria.format: Output is exactly one JSON object, no code fences, no prose, parseable as-is
scoring_criteria.domain_relevance: Reasoning references product-photo / grooming-submission context, not generic image description
scoring_criteria.clarity: reason field is a short, concrete justification
